text: Deinde Thapsam, et omnia, quae erant in ea, ejusque fines usque a Thersa, pervastavit Manahemus, quod ei portas non aperuerant, Thapsensesque gravidas mulieres omnes dilaniavit.
note: *Thapsēnsēsque* capital, the people of Thapsa (1738 *thapsensesque*), as the settled *Jezrælēns-*, *Bēthēlēnsis*, *Samarītān-*; no paragraph at the KJV's ¶ (15:13–16 is 72 words, Shallum's reign and its end) (reader r6, 2026-11-23)

text: Manahemo vita defuncto, successit in regnum Israelitarum Phacehia, filius ejus,
note: paragraph: Pekahiah; the sentence begins here and runs into 15:23 (*successit … Phacehia, fīlius ejus, annō Āzariæ … quīnquāgēsimō*); the draft's paragraph at 15:23, mid-sentence (the BSB's heading and the KJV's ¶ follow the Hebrew's sentences), moved here, as the settled 1 Kgs 16:28 *Ambrī vītā dēfūnctō … accēpit Achābus* and r5's 13:9; 1738 has no indent; 15:17–21 96 words, 15:22–26 69 (reader r6, 2026-11-23)

text: anno Azariae Judaeae regis quinquagesimo. Regnavit Samariae biennium.
note: no paragraph: the verse ends 15:22's sentence; moved to 15:22 (reader r6, 2026-11-23)

text: Hujus Phacae Israelitarum regis temporibus Theglathphalasar Assyriae rex, expeditione facta, cepit Ionem, et Abelmaacham, et Janoam, et Cadem, et Hasor, et Galaaditidem, et Galilaeam, et omnem tractum Nephthalensem, hominesque in Assyriam transtulit.
note: *Nephthālēnsem* capital (1738 *nephthalensem*), as the settled *Nephthālēnsem*, *Nephthālēnsium* (1 Kgs 15:20); *Iōnem* keeps its I, a vowel (Hebrew עִיּוֹן), as the settled 1 Kgs 15:20 *subēgit Iōnem et Danem, et Ābēlmaacham* (r6.md) (reader r6, 2026-11-23)

text: Jothamo vita defuncto, et apud majores suos in urbe Davidis, auctoris generis ejus, sepulto,
note: no paragraph: 1738's chapter 16 opens here (*IOthamo vita defuncto*), but the versification moved the chapter break to 16:1 inside the sentence (*… sepultō, Jūdææ rēgnum obtinuit Achazus*); the verse stays in 15:32's paragraph with its comma, as r5's 11:21 and the settled 1 Kgs 14:31 (reader r6, 2026-11-23)

text: Judaeae regnum obtinuit Achazus ejus filius, anno Phacae Romeliae filii decimo septimo,
note: paragraph at the chapter (the draft's `\nb` made `\p`), as r5's 12:1 and the settled 1 Kgs 3:1, 13:1, 15:1, 2 Sam 14:1, 20:1: 15:38 *Jōthamō vītā dēfūnctō … sepultō,* (1738's chapter opening) runs into *Jūdææ rēgnum obtinuit*; the BSB's heading here; 16:1–9 167 words (reader r6, 2026-11-23)

text: ut, Israeliticorum regum mores imitatus, etiam filium suum per ignem trajiceret: qualia sunt gentium flagitia, quas Jova ob Israelitas everterat:
note: *Isrāēlīticōrum* capital, an adjective of a people (1738 *israeliticorum*), as r3's 7:13, r5's 13:25 and the settled *Isrāēlītic-* (reader r6, 2026-11-23)

text: Quum enim totam regionem pervasisset: Samariam adortus triennium obsedit;
note: no paragraph: the draft's (the KJV's ¶, the BSB's heading) taken out, since Castellio's *Cum enim* explains 17:4 (how Salmanasar came to seize Hoshea) and the sentence then runs to 17:6 *collocāvit*; 1738 has no indent; 17:1–6 one paragraph of 97 words, the sermon beginning at 17:7 (a judgment: keeping it gives 66/31) (reader r6, 2026-11-23)

text: Et quia Israelitae contra Jovam Deum suum, a quo ex Aegypto deportati, et ex Pharaonis Aegypti regis potestate fuerant adserti, peccaverant, alienosque deos reveriti,
note: paragraph: why Israel was exiled, the period *Et quia … ob hæc, inquam, Jōva … īrātus* (17:7–18) beginning here after 17:6's full stop; the BSB's break (b), no KJV ¶; 1738 flush (no indent), so the paragraph is the edition's: 17:5–23 would be 358 words with 17:5's paragraph, now 17:1–6 97, 17:7–18 238, 17:19–23 89 (reader r6, 2026-11-23)

text: Ac Judaeis etiam, Jovae Dei sui praecepta non servantibus, sed introducta ab Israelitis instituta tenentibus:
note: paragraph: Judah too, and the Lord's rejection of all Israel (17:19–23, 89 words), a sentence start after 17:18's full stop (*relictā sōlā Jūdæōrum tribū.*); no KJV ¶ or indent; the BSB breaks at 17:18 (mid-sentence in Castellio) and 17:21 (*Nam sēparātī*, the alternative: 17:7–20 268, 17:21–23 59) (reader r6, 2026-11-23)

text: Deduxit autem rex Assyriae ex Babylone, Cutha, Ava, Hematha, et Sepharuaimo coloniam in oppida Samaritana, in locum Israelitarum, occupataque est a colonis, et habitata Samaria, atque ejus oppida.
note: the draft's paragraph kept (1738's indent, the KJV's ¶, the BSB's heading); *Samarītāna* capital (1738 *samaritana*), as the settled *Samarītāna*, *Samarītān-*; *Sepharuaimo* the draft's u/v slip (r6.md: *Sepharvaimo*), kept here for merge.py (reader r6, 2026-11-23)

text: Itaque demonstratum regi Assyriae est, colonos ab eo in oppida Samaritana deductos, quoniam Dei illius terrae naturam ignorarent: propterea, immissis ab illo leonibus, necari.
note: *Samarītāna* capital (1738 *samaritana*), as 17:24; the report reported (*dēmōnstrātum … necārī*), unmarked where the BSB quotes (reader r6, 2026-11-23)

text: Avani Nebahazum et Thartacum. Sepharuaimenses Adramelecho et Anamelecho diis Sepharuaimensibus filios suos igni cremabant.
note: *Sepharvaimēnsibus* capital, the adjective of the city's name (1738 *sepharuaimensibus*); *Sepharuaim-* the draft's u/v slip twice (r6.md), kept here for merge.py (reader r6, 2026-11-23)

text: Atque ad hunc diem pristinos ritus retinent, neque Jovae religionem tenent, neque instituta, jura, legem, disciplinam exsequuntur, quam Jova prognatis Jacobo (cui nomen imposuerat Israelis) tradidit,
